title: Raiders roundtable: How many games will the team win this year? - NewsBreak
text:
By Darrell Harris ,
13 hours ago
LAS VEGAS ( KLAS ) — The beginning of Las Vegas Raiders training camp signals the official return of the NFL. The upcoming season is the team’s seventh since relocating and excitement is perhaps at an all-time high.
Before the 8 News Now sports department attempts to predict the future, let’s revisit the Raiders’ rollercoaster of an offseason.
>>Watch Sports Wrap Daily at 5:30 p.m. on the 8 News+ streaming app The Kubiak era has begun After firing Pete Carroll in the wake of a 3-14 season , the team hired Klint Kubiak as head coach . Kubiak chose Las Vegas over other suitors fresh off winning the Super Bowl as offensive coordinator for the Seattle Seahawks. Arriving with him was nearly an entire new set of coaches, introducing several new schemes.
Raider Nation said goodbye to Maxx Crosby for a mere 48 hours. The shocking trade reversal with the Baltimore Ravens came as a bevy of free agent talent agreed to contracts with the Raiders, under the impression that Crosby was gone. General Manager John Spytek made the most of a messy situation, welcoming Crosby back while honoring all pre-existing deals.
In April, the team added Heisman quarterback Fernando Mendoza , fresh off winning a national championship with the Indiana Hoosiers. Weeks prior to the draft, however, the team added veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins .
Kubiak made it clear that Cousins will begin camp as the starter, while encouraging competition from the rookie Mendoza and Aidan O’Connell, who’s entering year four with the Raiders. Now it’s time to let the predictions fly!
Chris Maathuis: 8-9 The Raiders have reason for optimism. This rebuild appears to be sitting on a stronger foundation, but 2026 will be a bridge to bigger and better things. The QB room is the biggest story to follow. Kirk Cousins is a solid veteran who’s had success and seems eager to mentor rookie Fernando Mendoza. Ashton Jeanty will be the bell cow at running back. If the offensive line is solid, Jeanty will have a terrific year.
The receivers’ room is still a question mark. However, tight end Brock Bowers is in line for a big year similar to his Pro Bowl rookie season. Raider Nation is hoping Maxx Crosby returns to form as the best edge in the league. Given the difficult schedule, an eight-win season will be the best-case scenario, but 6-7 wins is probably more realistic.
Darrell Harris: 11-6 The team will need a strong first month, as the schedule gets rough quickly. A revamped offensive line should uplift the entire offense. If the interceptions and punts from last season can become field goals, touchdowns, or simply better field positioning – that’s half the battle. With Maxx Crosby playing beside a vastly improved defense, the Raiders are positioned to play complementary football on the way to their first winning season in years.
It’s no coincidence that Klint Kubiak, the most sought-after coaching candidate on the market, chose this Raiders team. GM John Spytek then worked wonders to improve the roster. The fanbase is ready for the Raiders to shock the world and live up to the rallying cry ‘Just win baby.’
Madyson Marie: 8-9 The Raiders will have a successful season this year if they can produce an explosive offense. From a new coaching staff to the new faces on offense, the Silver and Black have the opportunity to flip the narrative of the team in a high-scoring AFC West. Expect to see the Raiders focus on developing Fernando Mendoza into a franchise quarterback while watching Kirk Cousins complete his time in the league.
Vegas’ strength will come from their run game with both second-year running back Ashton Jeanty and rookie Mike Washington Jr. As for the defense, Las Vegas has added veterans and draft picks to the team’s already strong trenches. Fans could see Maxx Crosby play with a complementary second edge, something he’s rarely competed with.
Ron Futrell: 6-11 The biggest task for the Raiders this year is to protect their quarterback. It’s been the team’s main problem for years and years – they have good QBs, but they have to give them time. Another x-factor is the linebacker position. Moving to the 3-4 defense means Maxx Crosby will technically be a linebacker, who will still be a menace in the offensive backfield. Keep an eye on Tommy Eichenberg in this position. He was great on special teams last year and is making progress – watch No. 44!
Alexis Bass: 10-7 This season will be a success if the Raiders can quickly find rhythm on the ground and in the air. They’ll need a breakout year from one of the wide receivers, alongside major utilization of Brock Bowers and Ashton Jeanty again. Now it’s a matter of coming together to protect Kirk Cousins. If Kirk can find his own with his offensive weapons, that will also make a major difference. Seeing the marriage between Kubiak’s playcalling and Kirk’s execution should be fun, especially with the history that they have.
Regardless of who’s right and who’s wrong, tune into Sports Wrap Daily all season long as the season carries on. The 8 News Now team will be covering all sides of the team, alongside a rotating cast of experts and insiders along the way. Look for in-depth Raiders coverage every Friday at 5:30 p.m. on the free 8 News+ streaming app , with additional coverage throughout the week.
Last season, special guests included the likes of CBS’ James Brown, ESPN Radio host Q Myers, Jesse Merrick of the Silver & Black Sports Network, and Alain DeSaix of the Bleav network.
